concern.concern: Verification 1.1 says the real cosine and sine modes are orthonormal 'because they are the real and imaginary parts of the orthonormal character basis'. Raw real and imaginary parts have squared norm 1/2 under normalized Haar measure. The Example specifies normalized coefficients, so the conclusion is recoverable, but the verification should explicitly include the normalization factors.

concern.concern: Verification 1.1 asserts that the real Fourier modes are orthonormal 'by taking real and imaginary parts of the character basis'. Those parts require normalization: under normalized Haar measure, cos(nx) and sin(nx) have norm 1/√2. Specify the normalized real modes when identifying the canonical coefficient inner product with the function-space model.

original_verdict.reason: The n=1 conjugate update gives N(0,1/2); the likelihood is proportional to exp(-u²/2), so the pCN target and acceptance rule match. The stated assumptions and all β endpoints are covered by the cited invariance theorem.

concern.concern: The uniform needle bound lacks a uniform separation hypothesis. Step 1.2 says, “compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for |z-z′|,” but embeddedness for each ε and compact control of the critical-point charts do not prevent another regular strand from approaching the needle as ε→0. Locally take the fixed Morse cap z=s, t=−s², |s|≤ε/2, and another upward strand z=iε. The cap has horizontal diameter ε and its critical chart is unchanged. Its two signed degree-one mixed-chord integrals sum, up to orientation sign, to (2πi)⁻¹ log((1/2−i)/(−1/2−i)), a nonzero constant; the chord joins different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. These local pieces can be extended by regular arcs inside a fixed slab. Thus the written chart assumptions do not justify Cmε uniformly. The cited CDM §8.6.2 argument also uses opposite-branch cancellation rather than the claimed individual absolute long-chord estimate. The convergence assertion for a fixed tangle is a separate issue.
